cards.front: Individual account
cards.back: An account with one beneficial owner who is the only person who can control investments and request distributions. Upon death, assets pass through the owner's estate unless other arrangements (e.g., TOD) have been made.

cards.front: What is the key difference between Tenants in Common (TIC) and Joint Tenants with Right of Survivorship (JTWROS) accounts when one owner dies?
cards.back: TIC: the decedent's fractional interest passes to the decedent's estate. JTWROS: the decedent's interest passes to the surviving tenant(s). All JTWROS tenants have an undivided interest; TIC tenants each specify a percentage interest.

cards.front: A widow opens an account and wants any remaining assets to bypass probate and go directly to her two children at her death, while she retains full control during her lifetime. What account feature should be added?
cards.back: A Transfer on Death (TOD) designation. TOD avoids probate but does not avoid estate tax. It can be added to individual or JTWROS accounts (on JTWROS, it takes effect after the death of the last surviving tenant).

cards.front: What events terminate a power of attorney (POA), including a durable POA?
cards.back: The death of either party (the account owner/grantor or the appointed attorney). A durable POA continues through the incapacity of the grantor but still terminates at death.

cards.front: Distinguish a Full Power of Attorney (FPOA) from a Limited Power of Attorney (LPOA).
cards.back: FPOA: appointee can deposit/withdraw cash or securities and make investment decisions—essentially the same authority as the owner. LPOA (limited trading authorization): appointee can enter buy/sell orders only; no withdrawal of cash or securities.

cards.front: What documents must a corporation provide to open a brokerage account, and what is required to open a margin account?
cards.back: A corporate charter (proof of existence) and a corporate resolution (authorizing the account and naming officers who may trade). To open a margin account, the corporate charter must not prohibit margin trading.

cards.front: What documentation is required to open a partnership account, and what is required annually?
cards.back: A written partnership agreement specifying which partners may transact, plus authorization from the partners. An amended partnership agreement must be obtained each year if any changes have been made. If margin is desired, the partnership agreement must not prohibit it.

cards.front: Sole proprietor (d/b/a) account
cards.back: An account opened for a sole proprietor that may include a fictitious business name ("doing business as"). Checks may be made payable to either the owner or the business name. The account is effectively the property of the business owner.

cards.front: Identify the three roles in a trust and the function of each.
cards.back: Grantor (settlor): the person who creates and funds the trust with assets. Trustee: manages the trust assets for the beneficiary and owes a fiduciary duty. Beneficiary: receives the benefit of the trust assets.

cards.front: How does a revocable living trust differ from an irrevocable trust for estate tax purposes?
cards.back: Revocable trust: grantor retains control, may modify or revoke; assets remain part of the grantor's estate. Irrevocable trust: grantor gives up control and cannot modify; assets may be removed from the estate, but the grantor cannot serve as trustee or beneficiary.

cards.front: Living trust vs. decedent's trust
cards.back: Living trust: created and funded during the grantor's lifetime. Decedent's trust: funded through a will or estate process after the owner has died.

cards.front: Who is the beneficial owner of an UTMA/UGMA custodial account, and whose Social Security number is used?
cards.back: The minor is the beneficial owner. The account is registered under the minor's Social Security number, and all tax liability belongs to the minor (taxed at the minor's rate).

cards.front: List the key restrictions on a custodial (UGMA/UTMA) account.
cards.back: Cash account only—no margin and securities may not be pledged as collateral. One custodian and one minor per account. Cash/dividends must be reinvested within a reasonable time. No speculative investments (no naked options, no futures); covered call writing is generally permitted. Stock rights/warrants must be exercised or sold. Custodian may be reimbursed for expenses (and compensated only if not the donor).

cards.front: What are the principal differences between UGMA and UTMA accounts?
cards.back: UTMA permits real estate to be titled in custodial name; UGMA does not. UTMA accounts may be held in custodial name until the beneficiary is up to 25 (21 in some states); UGMA assets transfer at the state's age of majority. Nearly all states now use UTMA.

cards.front: The minor beneficiary of a UTMA account dies before reaching the age of majority. To whom do the securities pass?
cards.back: To the minor's estate—not to the custodian or to the parents (unless they are heirs of the minor's estate).

cards.front: State the contribution rules and tax treatment for a Coverdell Education Savings Account (ESA).
cards.back: After-tax contributions up to $2,000 per beneficiary per year until the beneficiary's age 18 (contribution limit phased out at higher incomes). Growth is tax-deferred; qualified distributions for K–12, secondary, or college expenses are tax-free. Nonqualified distributions are subject to income tax plus a 10% penalty on the earnings portion. Funds remaining at age 30 must be distributed (taxed + 10% penalty) or rolled to another family member's ESA.

cards.front: Name at least five types of fiduciaries who may open an account on behalf of another party.
cards.back: Trustee of a trust; executor of an estate; administrator (when decedent died intestate); guardian of a minor or incompetent; custodian (UGMA/UTMA); receiver in bankruptcy; conservator of an incompetent person.

cards.front: What is the "prudent investor rule" as it applies to fiduciary accounts, and may a fiduciary share in account profits?
cards.back: A fiduciary must make wise, safe investments consistent with the beneficiary's needs; speculative transactions are generally prohibited, and many states publish a "legal list" of approved securities. A fiduciary may not share in account profits but may charge a reasonable fee for services.

cards.front: Under what condition may a fiduciary account (including a trust account) be opened as a margin account?
cards.back: Only if margin trading is specifically authorized by the legal documents that establish the fiduciary relationship (e.g., the trust agreement).

cards.front: A customer wants the account statements to show only a number rather than her name because she is a public figure. Is this permitted?
cards.back: Yes—"numbered accounts" are permitted in exceptional cases for privacy (e.g., celebrities, politicians). The customer must sign a statement acknowledging ownership, and the member firm must maintain a record of the actual owner's identity.
